"50X The Cash" has one of six top prizes left and is close to selling out. Most of the tickets are already sold. As a game goes on, the same prizes are spread across fewer tickets. Right now, tickets and top prizes are running out at about the same rate.

If you play "50X The Cash" often, bookmark this page. The write-up is updated with each morning's data.
981.headline: How far along this game is

985.body:
MAX-A-MILLION's prizes make it a game with most of its money in small, frequent prizes. Of the prize money still unclaimed, most is in wins under $5,000. The prize counts change every day, but this design does not.

The second-biggest prize left on "MAX-A-MILLION" is $100,000, with six of them remaining.

Every line of MAX-A-MILLION's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
985.headline: How this game pays out

988.body:
The prize money on "Emerald 10's" leans toward small, frequent prizes. It is spread over eleven prize levels, from wins equal to the ticket price up to $1 million. Games built like this give out wins often, but rarely large ones. That design never changes, and it is the part you choose.

Every line of Emerald 10's's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
988.headline: How prizes are split

990.body:
The top prize count on "LADY LUCK" has not moved since we started watching it. The game still has two of four top prizes unclaimed. Smaller prizes keep getting claimed as tickets sell. The same top prizes are now among fewer tickets.

Today's free summary of "LADY LUCK" ends here. Every number behind it is on this page.
990.headline: No top prize claimed lately

992.body:
"$2 MILLION VAULT" has 132,614 prizes of $20 still unclaimed, which is its most common win. Just below the top prize is the $100,000 prize, with one left. The full count for every prize level is listed below.

The numbers for "$2 MILLION VAULT" will change a little by tomorrow, and this page will change with them.
992.headline: Prize table details

993.body:
About three-quarters of the tickets for "$5,000 Triple Play" are sold. The top prize count has held, with three of six still unclaimed. The number of tickets printed is fixed, so that is a plain good sign.

Everything above about "$5,000 Triple Play" comes from the North Carolina Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
993.headline: Tickets sell, top prizes remain

994.body:
"$25,000 Triple Play" has one of four top prizes left and is well into its run. About three-quarters of the tickets are already sold. As a game goes on, the same prizes are spread across fewer tickets. Right now, the top prizes and the tickets are going at about the same pace.

Tomorrow's count on "$25,000 Triple Play" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.
994.headline: Where this game is in its run

995.body:
Of all the tickets printed for "$200,000 Triple Play", about a quarter are still unsold. The game is well into its run, with two of four top prizes unclaimed. In every scratcher, either the tickets or the prizes run out first. The rest of this page shows the details.

The numbers for "$200,000 Triple Play" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
995.headline: Early stage or late

996.body:
"$1,000,000 Triple Play" is past the halfway point of its run, with about a third of its tickets still unsold. Late in a run, a game is worth a look when prizes outlast tickets. Early on, the prize design matters most. Here, the top prizes are being claimed more slowly than the tickets are selling, which is a good sign.

The numbers for "$1,000,000 Triple Play" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
996.headline: Early stage or late
